# @moku-labs/game

> 2D puzzle game engine on TypeScript, built as a Layer-2 framework on @moku-labs/core. The game is a deterministic graph of business logic. State commits only on edges. Position is data. Player input and world events are answers a node waits for. The screen is a projection of committed state. V1 is the logic plugins `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow` and a headless testing entry; V2 adds the screen plugins `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, a Pixi v8 renderer loaded lazily, and the `@moku-labs/game/assets` entry that generates typed asset keys. V3 adds the interface plugins `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui` (`screen` lists all nine) and the opt-in `audio`: choreographies as data, strings as data, text from MSDF fonts, screens in JSX laid out by Yoga, sound as an effect a node awaits. V4 adds two doors for the editor: `@moku-labs/game/inspect` reads a running game, `@moku-labs/game/control` drives a dev build. V5 adds the opt-in plugin `effects`: particles and WGSL/GLSL filters as components. V6 adds the opt-in plugin `platform`: the Back button, haptics and keep-awake through a provider the game passes. The game shell makes a game a folder of data: `@moku-labs/game/app` (`defineGameApp`, `config.ts` as `GameConfig`), the page `@moku-labs/game/app/page`, the system shell `@moku-labs/game/app/system` and the bin `moku-game` that serves, builds, packages and packs the folder. The package is published on npm as `@moku-labs/game`, and this file ships inside it.

Facts: Bun only. ESM only. `"sideEffects"` lists the root entry `./dist/index.mjs` only, every other entry has none. `pixi.js` `^8.0.0` is a peer dependency, no V1 code imports it. `playwright-core` (visual tests), `sharp` (the asset pack), `typescript` (the project index), `@moku-labs/system` (the system shell and the store save) and `@moku-labs/native` (`moku-game native`) are optional peers. Node >= 24, Bun >= 1.3.14. TypeScript strict with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. The engine ships no genre rules: no merge, no match-3, no physics. A game brings its own pure rule functions.

## Entry points

- `@moku-labs/game`: everything a game imports.
- `@moku-labs/game/app`: `defineGameApp`, `startMoment` and the types of a game's `index.ts` and `config.ts`. No `node:` import, no system or native package. See "The game shell".
- `@moku-labs/game/app/page` (the browser): `startPage`, the page the generated `.moku/main.ts` calls.
- `@moku-labs/game/app/system` (the browser, the native shell): `systemShellOf`, `fromSystem`, `storeSave`, `createSystemApp`, the type `SystemModules`, over the optional peer `@moku-labs/system`. The one entry that names it, in types only: the page hands it the loaders.
- `@moku-labs/game/cli` (node and bun only): `runCli`, the bin `moku-game`, `preparePage`, the editor's dev page, and `watchKeys`, the watch that keeps `generated/` fresh next to it.
- `@moku-labs/game/testing`: headless play, repro runs, isolated feature tests (`isolate`, `stub`), fake clock, in-memory save provider. No `node:` import.
- `@moku-labs/game/visual` (node and bun only): the visual tests `defineVisualTest`, `runVisualTests`, `parseVisualArgv`. The bin runs them: `moku-game visual`.
- `@moku-labs/game/assets` (node and bun only): the asset key scanner, the production packer and the string compiler. The package bin `moku-game-assets` runs it.
- `@moku-labs/game/inspect`: the read door of the editor, safe in a production build. See "Doors for the editor".
- `@moku-labs/game/control`: the write door of the editor, dev builds only. See "Doors for the editor".
- `@moku-labs/game/hot` (the Bun dev server only): the Bun plugin that hot swaps views in a running page; `moku-game dev` lists it. See "Hot swap".
- `@moku-labs/game/lint`: the oxlint JS plugin `moku-game` with the game lint rules. See "Lint for games".
- `@moku-labs/game/project` (node and bun only): the project index, where every engine id of a game is defined, line read fresh at the call. It follows the tsconfig `paths` of the game. The package bin `moku-game-index` runs it. See "Project index".
- `@moku-labs/game/fonts/*`: the shipped MSDF body font and its licence. See "Fonts".
- `@moku-labs/game/jsx-runtime` and `@moku-labs/game/jsx-dev-runtime`: what `"jsxImportSource": "@moku-labs/game"` resolves to. A game never imports them by hand.

Root exports:
- Functions: `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `defineGame`, `defineFeature`, `type`, `exit`, `to`, `slot`, `schedule`, `guide`, `hint`.
- Class: `SaveUnreadableError`.
- Plugin instances: `timePlugin`, `lifecyclePlugin`, `modelPlugin`, `clockPlugin`, `flowPlugin`, `worldPlugin`, `rendererPlugin`, `inputPlugin`, `assetsPlugin`, `scenesPlugin`, `animPlugin`, `i18nPlugin`, `textPlugin`, `uiPlugin`, `audioPlugin`, `effectsPlugin`, `platformPlugin`; the list `screen` = `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`. `effects`, `audio` and `platform` are opt-in: `plugins: [...screen, effectsPlugin, audioPlugin, platformPlugin]`, `platform` last.
- Screen helpers from the root: `component`, `tag`, `resource`, `mut`, `system`, `projection`, `Layer`, `Order`, `Exiting`, `Tree`, `Transform`, `Sprite`, `NineSlice`, `Shape`, `Parent`, `Display`, `sprite`, `Tappable`, `Pressable`, `Draggable`, `DropTarget`, `Swipeable`, `Traceable`, `Touchable`, `Held`, `Hovered`, `PointerOver`, `Pressed`, `Pointer`, `Traced`, `defineBundles`, `load`, `defineScene`.
- Interface helpers from the root (V3): `defineAnimation`, `sequence`, `parallel`, `stagger`, `tween`, `set`, `wait`, `mark`, `frames`, `sfx`, `haptic`, `use`, `spawn`, `spawned`, `play`, `external`, `defineMotion`, `Animation`, `Frames`, the resource `AnimPlayer`; `tr`, `messageArgument`, `messageDuration`; `Text`, `label`, `defineTextStyles`, `bind`, `Countdown` and the types `BindOptions`, `CountdownValue`, `TextFormat`; `defineComponent`, `popup`, `defineStyle`, `defineTokens`, `resolve`, `Box`, `LocalWrite`; `music`.
- Effects helpers from the root (V5): `defineEmitter`, `Emitter`, `defineFilter`, `Glow`, `Outline`, `Blur`, `ColorMatrix`, `Noise`, `Displacement`, `Alpha`.
- Platform from the root (V6): the types `PlatformProvider`, `BackResult`, `HapticKind` and the frozen list `HAPTIC_KINDS`.
- `defineGame<Types>()` returns, typed by the game's `player`, `session`, `assets`, `bundles`, `scenes`, `strings` and `textStyles`: `defineNode`, `defineFlow`, `defineFeature`, `projection`, `sprite`, `Sprite`, `NineSlice`, `defineBundles`, `load`, `defineScene`, `defineAnimation`, `frames`, `sfx`, `play`, `tr`, `label`, `defineTextStyles`, `defineComponent`, `defineStyle`, `defineTokens`, `popup`, `music`, `Frames`, `defineEmitter`, `Emitter`, `Displacement`. `Types` is `{ player; session; assets: string; bundles?: string; scenes?: string; strings: Record<string, unknown>; textStyles?: string; emitters?: string }`.
- `@moku-labs/game/assets`: `scanAssets(options)`, `emitKeys`, `emitManifest`, `compileStrings(root, out, options?)`, `checkStrings`, `packAssets(options)`, `exportStrings`, `importStrings`, `runCli(argv, strings)` with `strings: StringsTools` = `{ compile: compileStrings, exportStrings, importStrings }`. Audio files are `.mp3` or `.m4a`. Asset key = feature (or layer name) + "." + path inside `assets/`. `runCli` (a game's `bun run assets:keys`) scans the assets and compiles `features/*/strings/<locale>.json`, and the `strings/` of every layer, into `generated/strings.ts` (the `Strings` type for `defineGame`) and one `generated/strings.<locale>.ts` per locale (it imports `messageArgument` and `messageDuration` from `@moku-labs/game` when a message needs them, no helper is copied in); `--check` fails when any output is out of date; `--pack <dir>` writes the production build. `--layer <folder>[=<name>]`, repeatable and good with every mode, scans `<root>/<folder>/` like one more feature under `<name>` (`<folder>` alone maps to itself): its `assets.ts`, `assets/` and `strings/<locale>.json`. A game on the layered layout passes `--layer shared=ui`, so `shared/assets/*` keeps the `ui.*` keys. A missing layer folder is a warning. `scanAssets`, `compileStrings`, `exportStrings` and `importStrings` take the same map as `layers: { shared: "ui" }`. `--pseudo` also writes the pseudo-locale `en-XA`. `--export <dir>` and `--import <dir>` exchange strings with translators; `--source <locale>` names the locale they read from, `"en"` by default. The package bin `moku-game-assets` is this CLI: a script is `"assets:keys": "moku-game-assets --root src --manifest public/assets/manifest.json --keys src/generated/assets.ts"`. A game with `config.ts` runs `moku-game keys` and `moku-game pack` instead: they pass its paths and its layers.
- Type namespaces: `Time`, `Lifecycle`, `Model`, `Clock`, `Flow`, `World`, `Renderer`, `Input`, `Assets`, `Scenes`, `Anim`, `I18n`, `TextTypes`, `Ui`, `Audio`, `Effects`, `Platform`. Use `import type { Flow } from "@moku-labs/game"` and then `Flow.RouteStep`, `Flow.NodeContext`, `Model.Json`, `Model.PlayerStateProvider`, `Clock.ClockSource`, `Time.Phase`, `Lifecycle.PauseReason`, `Anim.Target`, `I18n.Message`. `Text` is the component, so the text types are `TextTypes`.
- `defineNode` and `defineFlow` are NOT root exports. They come from `defineGame<Types>()`.

## Concepts

- Node: a small function with a plain `await` body. It gets one context object and returns `out.<outcome>(payload)`. A bare string is not accepted.
- Flow: an id, a `nodes` table, a `start` node and an `edges` table. One entry per outcome of every node. The compiler checks the table.
- Exactly one node is active. The runner opens one model transaction per node run and commits it on the edge. A node that throws changes nothing.
- Transit node: has `run`, no `rest`. Rest node: `rest: true`. The graph waits there. Without `run` it is a pure wait.
- A pure wait ends in two ways. A gate answer whose `intent` is an outcome name: the answer payload becomes the outcome payload. Or a world event whose `type` is listed in the node's `inbox`: the event payload becomes the outcome payload.
- Transition: rest node to rest node. It is a transaction. On an error the runner discards, rolls back to the last rest point, retries `retries` times, then enters `safeNode`. A failure inside `safeNode` rejects `run()`.
- Entering a rest node calls `model.store.markRest()`: the save provider gets the patches. Leaving a `barrier` node calls `markBarrier(txId)`: a durable write, and rollback cannot cross it.
- `checkpoint: true` on a rest node: the journal is compacted there. `safeNode` must be a checkpoint.
- `over: true`: entering the node waits while a pointer is down.
- Path: node names joined by `/` through sub-flows and slots. Examples: `"home"`, `"board/awaitIntent"`, `"afterBonus/thanks"`.
- Edge target: a node name, `exit(...)` or `to(...)`. A payload must fit the input of the target. A node without input accepts any payload.
- Sub-flow: a flow that declares `outcomes` is used as a node of another flow. `exit("name")` leaves it with that outcome.
- Slot: `slot("name")` is a node with the single outcome `done`. Features contribute sub-flows to it. They run in `order`. `when(snapshot)` can skip one; it always reads the committed state, also what an earlier contribution of the same slot wrote. A contribution may hold a slot of its own. The slot ends with its own `done` edge after the last contribution.
- Feature: `defineFeature(name, description)` makes an ordinary plugin that registers into `flow.features` in `onInit`. Pass it in `createApp({ plugins: [...] })`. `feature.logicOnly` is the same plugin with the V1 keys only, for headless tests.
- Modes: `"live"` and `"fast"`. In fast mode effects answer instantly, hints are dropped and only `runInFast` handlers run. All node logic runs for real.

## Authoring helpers, with signatures

```ts
function defineGame<Types extends Flow.GameTypes>();  // returns the helpers listed under "Root exports", typed by Types
// GameTypes = { player: Json; session: Json; assets: string; strings: Record<string, unknown>;
//               bundles?: string; scenes?: string; textStyles?: string; emitters?: string }

function type<Payload = void>(): TypeTag<Payload>;

// From the kit. Input and Tags are inferred from the spec.
defineNode(spec: {
  input?: TypeTag<Input>;
  outcomes: Tags;                      // { done: type(), failed: type<{ reason: string }>() }
  rest?: boolean;                      // run is required unless rest: true
  over?: boolean;
  checkpoint?: boolean;
  barrier?: boolean;
  inbox?: readonly (keyof Tags & string)[];
  run?: (ctx: NodeContext) => Result | Promise<Result>;
}): NodeDefinition;

defineFlow(id: string, spec: {
  nodes: Nodes;                        // node, sub-flow or slot per name
  start: string;                       // a node whose input accepts the flow input
  edges: Table;                        // edges[node][outcome] = target
  input?: TypeTag<Input>;
  outcomes?: FlowTags;                 // declare them to use the flow as a node
}): FlowDefinition;

function exit<const Name extends string>(outcome: Name): Exit<Name>;
function to<const TargetName extends string, Payload, Output>(
  target: TargetName,
  map: (payload: Payload) => Output    // annotate the parameter type yourself
): Mapped<TargetName, Payload, Output>;
function slot(name: string): SlotNode;

function defineFeature(name: string, description: FeatureDescription): FeaturePlugin;
// FeatureDescription = {
//   nodes?: readonly AnyNode[];
//   flows?: readonly AnyFlow[];
//   contribute?: Record<string, { flow: AnyFlow; order: number; when?: (snapshot: Snapshot) => boolean }>;
//   projections?, systems?, components?, scenes?, assets?;   // V2 keys, read by world, scenes and assets
//   animations?: readonly AnimationDefinition[];              // V3, read by anim
//   ui?: readonly ComponentDefinition[];                      // V3, read by ui (defineComponent results)
//   strings?: Record<locale, CompiledMessages | (() => Promise<unknown>)>;   // V3, read by i18n
//   textStyles?: ReturnType<typeof defineTextStyles>;         // V3, read by text
//   emitters?: readonly ReturnType<typeof defineEmitter>[];   // V5, read by effects
//   filters?: readonly ReturnType<typeof defineFilter>[];     // V5, read by effects
// }

function schedule(moment: number | undefined): Descriptor;  // awaited, asks the clock for one `elapsed`
function guide(options: GuideOptions): Descriptor;          // awaited, narrows the gate to one answer
function hint(kind: string, payload?: Json): Hint;          // for fx.emit, cosmetic
// GuideOptions = { allow: { intent: string; payload?: Json }; highlight?: readonly string[]; hand?: "tap" | "drag"; text?: string }
// Descriptor   = { kind: string; payload?: Json; answers?: readonly string[]; cosmetic?: boolean }
```

## Node context

```ts
type NodeContext = {
  input: Input;          // payload of the edge that led here
  player: Player;        // draft of the saved player tree, mutate it
  session: Session;      // draft of the session tree, never saved
  rng: RngView;          // rng.stream(id) gives a deterministic stream
  fx: NodeFx;            // await fx(descriptor), fx.emit(hint(...))
  out: Out;              // one method per declared outcome
  signal: AbortSignal;   // aborted on stop, restore and inbox delivery
  now: number;           // clock.now() read once at node entry
};
```

`RngStream` methods, integers only: `int(maxExclusive)`, `range(min, maxInclusive)`, `pick(items)`, `weighted(table)` with `{ weight: number }` entries, `chance(numerator, denominator)`.

## Rules of determinism

- Never call `Date.now()`, `performance.now()` or `new Date()` in a node or in rule functions. Use `now` from the node context.
- Never call `Math.random()`. Use `rng.stream("some-id")`. Use one id per source, for example `"chest:42"`. Stream state is part of the save, so a draw commits and rolls back with its transaction.
- Never call `setTimeout` or `setInterval` in game logic. Store the due moment in `player`, then `await fx(schedule(moment))` and wait for `elapsed` at a rest node with `inbox: ["elapsed"]`.
- State is plain JSON only. No classes, no `Map`, no `Date`, no `undefined` values in trees.
- Change state only through `player` and `session` of the node context. Do not keep game state in module scope or closures.
- Keep rules as pure functions `(state, input, tables) => result`. The node calls the rule and writes the result into the draft.
- A node never calls `app.model`, `app.clock` or `app.time`. Everything outside logic goes through `fx`.
- A timer is a moment stored in player state. How long is left is computed from `now`.

## Lint for games

`.oxlintrc.json` of a game (oxlint 1.86.0 or later). The engine ships no default severity: a game turns each rule on.

```json
{
  "jsPlugins": ["@moku-labs/game/lint"],
  "rules": {
    "moku-game/lazy-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/native-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/dev-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/no-module-state": "error",
    "moku-game/determinism": "error",
    "moku-game/rules-siblings": "error",
    "moku-game/static-keys": "error",
    "moku-game/layer-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/feature-door": "error",
    "moku-game/test-suffix": "error"
  }
}
```

- `moku-game/lazy-imports` (L2): no static value import of `pixi.js` or `yoga-layout`. `import type` and `import()` pass. Default files `**`.
- `moku-game/native-imports` (L13): no `@moku-labs/system`, `@moku-labs/native`, `@tauri-apps/*` in the logic, the root `index.ts` and `config.ts`, `kit.ts` and `plugins/`. A game imports no native package: it names the capability in `config.ts` `system`, and the engine page wires it.
- `moku-game/dev-imports`: `@moku-labs/editor` and `@moku-labs/game/control` only in `*.dev.ts(x)`, tests and the generated `.moku/` page (and `web/main.ts`, `web/dev*.ts`, `web/editor*.ts` of a game that still has `web/`).
- `moku-game/no-module-state` (L5): no module-scope `let` or `var`, no module-scope `new Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet`. Default files `**`.
- `moku-game/determinism` (L3): no `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `new Date()`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` in the logic. `new Date(now)` passes. Plugin folders, `**/{plugin,plugins}/**`, are the effect side and are skipped: a plugin answers `schedule` with a timer.
- `moku-game/rules-siblings` (L4): a file under `rules/` imports only `./` siblings, `@core/types` and `@shared/rules`, by alias or by relative path. `@core/kit`, `../tables` and `import type … from "@moku-labs/game"` are reported.
- `moku-game/static-keys`: a JSX `key` is a literal, a template of such parts, `props.id` or `props.<name>Key`, a call, or a `const` of one. `tabKeys[props.tab]`, `a ?? b`, `a || b`, `a ? b : c` and `props.tab` are reported: pass the key in as a prop, `<TabButton id="tabSound" />`. Default files `**/*.tsx`.
- `moku-game/layer-imports`: the order is core ← shared ← features ← `game.ts`; plugins import core and shared; every layer may import `generated/`. An import, export-from or `import()` that reaches a layer above its own is reported, `import type` too: `@features/home` from `shared/`. Only `game.ts` imports `game.ts`.
- `moku-game/feature-door`: another feature is imported only through its `index.ts`, `@features/orders`, never `@features/orders/flow/merge`. Only `game.ts` imports the barrels `@features` and `@plugins`. A feature does not import its own `index.ts`. A relative import that leaves the feature is written as an alias: `@features/<f>`, `@shared`, `@core/<file>`. Inside one feature any relative import passes.
- `moku-game/test-suffix`: a file in a test kind folder ends with its suffix. `tests/e2e/` `.e2e.ts`, `tests/visual/` `.visual.ts`, `tests/editor/` `.editor.ts`, `__tests__/`, `__tests__/unit/` and `__tests__/integration/` `.test.ts`, `__tests__/isolated/` `.isolated.ts`, `__tests__/visual/` `.visual.ts`; a `.tsx` file adds an `x`. An `index.ts` of a kind folder passes, such as `tests/visual/index.ts` of `moku-game visual`. Helpers go to `tests/helpers/` or `__tests__/fixtures/`.
- Layers under the game root: `core/**`, `shared/**`, `features/<f>/**`, `plugins/<p>/**`, `generated/**`, `game.ts`, `tests/**`. A file outside them (`kit.ts`, `nodes/`, `web/`) keeps the layout rules quiet, so a game on the template layout lints as before.
- Aliases: `layer-imports`, `feature-door` and `rules-siblings` read the `compilerOptions.paths` of `tsconfig.json` (comments, trailing commas and relative `extends` included), the way the project index does. Without `paths` they read the v15 table: `@core/*` → `core/*`, `@shared` → `shared/index.ts`, `@shared/rules` → `shared/rules/index.ts`, `@features` → `features/index.ts`, `@features/*` → `features/*/index.ts`, `@plugins` → `plugins/index.ts`, `@generated/*` → `generated/*`, `@tests/*` → `tests/*`. `aliasTargetsOf(tsconfig, root, specifier)` from `@moku-labs/game/lint` answers what they read: for a game without a tsconfig, `aliasTargetsOf("/game/tsconfig.json", "/game", "@features/orders")` is `["/game/features/orders/index.ts"]`.
- Logic = the root `index.ts`, `**/state.ts`, `**/tables.ts`, `**/game.ts`, `**/{core,nodes,flows,rules,features,shared}/**`. Tests (`tests/**`, `**/__tests__/**`, `*.test.ts`) are skipped by every rule but `test-suffix`.
- Every rule takes `["error", { "files": [...], "ignores": [...] }]`. Globs are relative to the directory oxlint runs in; a key given replaces the default. `layer-imports`, `feature-door` and `rules-siblings` also take `root` (the folder of `core/`, `shared/`, `features/`, `plugins/` and `game.ts`, default `.`) and `tsconfig` (default `tsconfig.json`); `test-suffix` takes `root` and `suffixes` (kind folder to suffix, replaces the table whole).

## Minimal game

```ts
// state.ts
import { defineGame } from "@moku-labs/game";

export type Player = { coins: number; lastRoll: number };
export type Session = { rolls: number };

export const { defineNode, defineFlow, defineFeature } = defineGame<{
  player: Player;
  session: Session;
  assets: string;
  strings: Record<string, unknown>;
}>();
```

```ts
// nodes.ts
import { type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineNode } from "./state";

export const home = defineNode({
  outcomes: { roll: type() },
  rest: true,
  checkpoint: true
});

export const roll = defineNode({
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  run: ({ player, session, rng, out }) => {
    const face = rng.stream("dice").range(1, 6);

    player.coins += face;
    player.lastRoll = face;
    session.rolls += 1;
    return out.done();
  }
});
```

```ts
// flow.ts
import { defineFlow } from "./state";
import { home, roll } from "./nodes";

export const mainFlow = defineFlow("main", {
  nodes: { home, roll },
  start: "home",
  edges: {
    home: { roll: "roll" },
    roll: { done: "home" }
  }
});
```

```ts
// index.ts: the game as one data object
import { defineGameApp } from "@moku-labs/game/app";
import { mainFlow } from "./flow";

export default defineGameApp({
  flow: mainFlow,
  safeNode: "home",
  player: { coins: 0, lastRoll: 0 },
  session: { rolls: 0 }
});
```

```ts
// config.ts: the page, as plain data
import type { GameConfig } from "@moku-labs/game/app";

export default { page: { title: "Dice" } } satisfies GameConfig;
```

The game never calls `flow.run()`. The page runs the graph after `app.start()`; a test hands the app to `createHeadless`, which runs it. The screen sends answers with `app.flow.gate.answer({ intent: "roll" })`.

## The game shell

A game is a folder: `index.ts` (`export default defineGameApp({ ... })`), `config.ts` (plain data, `satisfies GameConfig`), `core/`, `shared/`, `features/`, `plugins/`, `generated/`, `tests/` with `tests/scenarios/<name>.ts`. No `web/`, no `native.ts`, no `platform-bridge.ts`, no `bunfig.toml`, no `createApp` call. `.moku/` holds what `moku-game` writes; the game's `.gitignore` lists it. Scripts of the game's `package.json`: `"dev": "moku-game dev"`, `"build": "moku-game build"`, `"native:ios-sim": "moku-game native build ios --simulator"`.

- `defineGameApp(definition)` returns the game, `{ headless(seams?), screen(seams?) }`, and creates no app. Every type comes from the object; no generic at the call site. Keys: `flow` (required), `safeNode` (default: the start of the main flow), `player` and `session` (required), `referenceLong` (1920), `seed` (42), `shared` (composed first among the features), `features`, `plugins` (their APIs land on `screen().app`), `headless: { features?, plugins? }`, `pluginConfigs`.
- `pluginConfigs` takes every plugin of the screen app but the keys the shell writes. A seam-owned key is a compile error: `model.playerProvider`, `initialPlayer`, `initialSession`, `seed` (the game keeps `schemaVersion`, `migrations`); all of `clock` and `platform`; `flow.mainFlow`, `safeNode`; `renderer.mount`; `assets.manifest`, `io`; `audio.context`.
- `game.headless(seams?)` composes the core plugins, `logicOnly` of `headless.features`, then `headless.plugins`. `game.screen(seams?)` composes the screen set, `audio`, `effects`, `platform`, then `shared`, the features and the game's plugins. Both return `{ app, clock, provider }`, the app not started; each call is fresh. Defaults: `fakeClock(startMoment)` (`startMoment` is `1_000_000`), a fresh `memory()` save, the seed of the definition or 42.
- Seams of both: `seed`, `clock`, `provider`, `player`, `session`. Screen only: `manifest` (a URL or the parsed file), `io`, `platform`, `keepAwake` (false), `audio: { context?, journal? }`, `renderer: { mount?, loadPixi?, preference? }`. Without a mount the renderer is inert, so `game.screen()` runs in plain Bun.
- `defineGameApp` throws `[game] defineGameApp needs flow.` and `[game] defineGameApp: features[2] is not a feature.` for what TypeScript cannot stop.
- A game's exit plugin calls `ctx.require(platformPlugin).exit()` itself.

```ts
// a test of the dice game
import { startMoment } from "@moku-labs/game/app";
import { createHeadless } from "@moku-labs/game/testing";
import game from "./index";

const { app, clock, provider } = game.headless();
const run = await createHeadless(app);

run.state().path; // "home"
clock.now() === startMoment; // true
provider.calls.map(call => call.method); // ["load", "commit"]: a new player
await run.walk([{ at: "home", intent: "roll" }, { at: "home", intent: "roll" }]);
app.model.store.snapshot().session; // { rolls: 2 }
await run.stop();
```

`config.ts` keys and defaults: `page.title` (required, never empty), `page.lang` (`"en"`), `page.background` (`"#000000"`: the page behind the canvas, the `theme-color` meta and the native window; the canvas clear colour stays `pluginConfigs.renderer.background`), `page.orientation` (`"portrait"`, or `"landscape"`, `"any"`: the native build locks it), `page.icons: { favicon?, appleTouch? }` (files relative to the game, `<link>` tags), `page.head` (raw tags, verbatim), `native: { name, identifier, icon?, targets? }` (absent: no native build), `system` (`[]`; names `lifecycle`, `back`, `haptics`, `keepAwake`, `store`), `save` (`"memory"`, or `"local"`, `"store"`), `assets.layers` (`{}`; `{ shared: "ui" }` becomes `--layer shared=ui`). A refused value throws, for example `[game] config.save is "disk".` or `[game] config.system names "tray", which the game shell does not wire.`

```ts
// config.ts of a game in a native shell
import type { GameConfig } from "@moku-labs/game/app";

export default {
  page: { title: "Лесной городок", lang: "ru", background: "#10161d", orientation: "portrait", icons: { favicon: "assets/icon.png" } },
  native: { name: "Лесной городок", identifier: "com.mokulabs.timber", icon: "assets/icon.png" },
  system: ["lifecycle", "back", "haptics", "keepAwake"],
  save: "memory",
  assets: { layers: { shared: "ui" } }
} satisfies GameConfig;
```

The page. `moku-game dev` and `build` write a `main.ts` that calls `startPage(game, config, { scenarios?, system?, agents?, devModules? })`. In order it resolves the config; picks the start; builds the system shell when the page has one and picks the save; makes `game.screen()` with the canvas on `#game`, `manifest.json` next to the page, the device clock and the shell's platform; sets `globalThis.game` (the app), `globalThis.system` (the system app or `undefined`) and `globalThis.doors` (`read`, `watch`, `sources`; `run`, `commands` in dev); follows reduced motion; starts the shell, the app, and runs the graph (a stop is logged `[game] The graph stopped.`); in dev starts the agents with `{ app, name, modules }`.
- `?player=<name>` starts from the scenario `tests/scenarios/<name>.ts` on a fresh memory save, never on the stored one. An unknown name logs `[game] No scenario "<name>".` and starts from the starting player. A scenario is `Scenario<Player>`: `(now) => ({ player, session? })`, its default export.
- `?renderer=webgl` asks Pixi for WebGL.
- Save kinds: `"memory"` lives for the page only; `"local"` is `localStorage` under `<native.identifier>:save` or `moku-game:save`, and falls back to memory with a warning where storage is refused; `"store"` is the system store (idb on the web, the Tauri store native), needs the shell, rejects a load it cannot read instead of starting a new player.
- System: the generated `main.ts` imports `systemShellOf` of `@moku-labs/game/app/system` only when `system` is not empty or `save` is `"store"`, so a web-only page bundles no system code. It passes `system: systemShellOf({ system: () => import("@moku-labs/system"), haptics: () => import("@moku-labs/system/haptics") })`: one loader per named plugin, in the order `lifecycle`, `back`, `haptics`, `keepAwake` (entry `keep-awake`), `store` (when named or `save` is `"store"`). The engine holds no `import()` of the package, so the page bundles only the named plugins: a game with `system: ["haptics"]` and a memory save builds without `@tauri-apps/plugin-store`. A loader that rejects: `[game] config.system needs @moku-labs/system.` with `bun add @moku-labs/system@^0.3.1`. A named plugin without a loader: `[game] config.system names "<name>", but main.ts has no loader for it.`

```ts
// .moku/main.ts of the engine's mini game, written by moku-game dev
// Written by moku-game dev. Do not edit.
import "./dev.ts";
import "./assets-stamp.ts";
import { startPage } from "@moku-labs/game/app/page";
import game from "../index.ts";
import config from "../config.ts";
import scenario0 from "../tests/scenarios/ready.ts";

await startPage(game, config, {
  scenarios: { "ready": scenario0 }
});
```

Commands of the bin `moku-game` (bun). Every command takes `--root <dir>` (default `.`), `--preload <path>` and `--serve-plugin <path>` (both repeat), before or after the command word. Exit 0 on success, else 1 with a `[game] …` line.
- `moku-game dev [--port 3000] [--packed]`: writes `.moku/index.html`, `dev.ts`, `main.ts`, `assets-stamp.ts`, `bunfig.toml` (the hot plugin first, `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__` defined `true`), runs Bun again under that bunfig in the game folder and serves `/`. It prints `› <folder>: dev server, raw assets. Ctrl+C stops it.` and then the bound URL alone on its own line, `http://localhost:3000/`. `--port 0` takes a free port. `--packed` serves `dist/assets`. A new or removed file in `tests/scenarios/` rewrites `main.ts`. On the raw files it keeps `generated/` fresh: it runs the scan of `keys` once before the page is written, and a save of an asset file (`.png`, `.webp`, `.fnt`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`) or of a `strings/<locale>.json` runs it again 100 ms after the last file event and prints `› keys: <path>` or `› keys: <path> and <n> more`; a changed or new string hot swaps through `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`, an asset file saved with new bytes swaps in the running page and a new or removed one reloads it, both through `.moku/assets-stamp.ts`, which `main.ts` imports (see "Hot swap"), and files answer `Cache-Control: no-store`. A failed scan is one warning `[game] keys: <message>` and the server runs on. A changed layer in `config.ts` needs a restart; `--packed` watches nothing. A taken port: `[game] dev: port 3000 is in use.` with `Pass --port 0 for a free port.`
- `moku-game build [--out dist/web]`: packs the assets, bundles the page minified with `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__` defined `false` (no scenario, no agent, no `.dev` module, no `/control`), every link `./`, and copies the pack beside it with `manifest.json` next to `index.html`. Runs from any http sub-path and from Tauri, not from `file://`.
- `moku-game native build <target> [--simulator]`, `native dev <target>`, `native doctor [<target>]`, `native clean [<target>]`: one verb of `@moku-labs/native` (a dev dependency, `^0.3.2`) over `config.ts`. App name, identifier and icon from `native`, orientation and background colour from `page`; the web build is `moku-game build`, the dev server `moku-game dev --port 5173`; system rows for `back`, `haptics`, `store`; the Tauri project in `.moku/tauri`, the apps in `dist-native`. `[game] config.ts has no native section.` without `native`.
- `moku-game keys [--check]`: `generated/assets.ts`, the compiled strings and the dev manifest `generated/manifest.json`; `dev` runs the same scan at start and on save and serves the manifest on `/manifest.json`, `visual` stops without it. `moku-game pack [--no-cache]`: `dist/assets`. Both pass the layers of `config.ts`.
- `moku-game visual [--update] [--only <name>] [--no-pixels | --pixels] [--webgl] [--dir <path>] [--tests <file>] [--url <url>]`: runs `runVisualTests` with the default export of `tests/visual/index.ts`, `{ app, tests }` (`app` is a `VisualSetup` `{ app, page? }`: `export default { app: { app: fixtureApp }, tests }`), against `tests/visual/baselines/`. The flags go through `parseVisualArgv`. The pixel leg runs on a Mac only unless `--pixels`/`--no-pixels`; without `--url` the command writes its own page into `.moku/visual/` (the page of `dev` and of the editor in `.moku/` stays), runs Bun again under `.moku/visual/bunfig.toml` as `dev` does (hot plugin, `--serve-plugin`, `--preload`), and the child serves the page on a free port, then stops it. No `manifest.json`: `[game] visual: no manifest.json in "<game>".` Exit 0 when the report is ok, else 1. `[game] visual: <file> must export default { app, tests }.` for a missing module or another shape, a bare app factory too.
- `preparePage(root, { agents?, preload?, servePlugins? })` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` writes the dev page of `moku-game dev` and resolves `{ html, bunfig }`, both absolute, for a server the caller starts: `bun --config=<bunfig>`. With agents the page also imports the game's `**/*.dev.ts` and hands them to the agents. It also writes the first, empty `.moku/assets-stamp.ts` when the game has none. The editor calls it: `await preparePage("games/timber", { agents: ["@moku-labs/editor/agent/page"] })`.
- `watchKeys(root, { onError? })` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` is the keys watch of `moku-game dev` for a server the caller runs: it runs the scan of `keys` once, resolves `{ close() }` after it, then scans again on a save of an asset or a strings file. A failed scan calls `onError(message)` (default: a console warning `[game] keys: <message>`) and the watch goes on. The editor calls it next to `preparePage`: `const keys = await watchKeys("games/timber", { onError: message => log.warn(message) })`, then `keys.close()`. It rejects with the `[game]` errors of `preparePage` for a folder that is not a game.

## More patterns

```ts
import { exit, hint, schedule, slot, to, type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineFeature, defineFlow, defineNode } from "./state";

// Awaited effect with answers. The gate opens for these intents. The promise resolves with the answer.
export const confirmReset = defineNode({
  outcomes: { yes: type(), no: type() },
  over: true,
  run: async ({ fx, out }) => {
    const answer = (await fx({ kind: "popup", payload: { name: "reset" }, answers: ["yes", "no"] })) as {
      intent: string;
    };

    return answer.intent === "yes" ? out.yes() : out.no();
  }
});

// Timer: arm the clock, emit a cosmetic hint, then wait for `elapsed` at a rest node.
export const arm = defineNode({
  outcomes: { armed: type() },
  run: async ({ now, fx, out }) => {
    await fx(schedule(now + 60_000));
    fx.emit(hint("sparkle", { target: "dice" }));
    return out.armed();
  }
});

export const waiting = defineNode({
  outcomes: { elapsed: type<{ now: number }>(), skip: type() },
  rest: true,
  inbox: ["elapsed"]
});

// Sub-flow with a mapped edge and two exits.
const pick = defineNode({ outcomes: { picked: type<{ face: number }>(), back: type() }, rest: true });
const apply = defineNode({
  input: type<{ value: number }>(),
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  run: ({ input, player, out }) => {
    player.coins += input.value;
    return out.done();
  }
});

export const bonusFlow = defineFlow("bonus", {
  nodes: { pick, apply },
  start: "pick",
  outcomes: { finished: type(), left: type() },
  edges: {
    pick: { picked: to("apply", (payload: { face: number }) => ({ value: payload.face * 2 })), back: exit("left") },
    apply: { done: exit("finished") }
  }
});

// Main flow with the sub-flow as a node and a slot.
const lobby = defineNode({ outcomes: { bonus: type() }, rest: true, checkpoint: true });

export const main = defineFlow("main", {
  nodes: { lobby, bonus: bonusFlow, afterBonus: slot("afterBonus") },
  start: "lobby",
  edges: {
    lobby: { bonus: "bonus" },
    bonus: { finished: "afterBonus", left: "lobby" },
    afterBonus: { done: "lobby" }
  }
});

// Feature: contributes a sub-flow to the slot. A feature name must differ from every flow id.
const thanks = defineNode({ outcomes: { ok: type() }, rest: true, over: true });
const thanksFlow = defineFlow("thanksPopup", {
  nodes: { thanks },
  start: "thanks",
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  edges: { thanks: { ok: exit("done") } }
});

export const thanksFeature = defineFeature("thanks", {
  flows: [thanksFlow],
  contribute: { afterBonus: { flow: thanksFlow, order: 10 } }
});
```

A tutorial step is `await fx(guide({ allow: { intent: "roll" }, hand: "tap", text: "Tap the dice" }))`. Only that answer passes the gate until the node exits.

## Graph rules checked at `run()`

- Every outcome of every node has an edge. Every edge names a node of the same flow or a declared flow outcome.
- The start node is in `nodes`. Every node is reachable from the start node.
- A cycle needs at least one rest node.
- Every `inbox` type is an outcome of its node. A rest node has outcomes or a `run` body.
- Every edge of a `barrier` node leads to a rest node of the same flow.
- Flow ids are unique. A feature name is not a flow id. It is also not a plugin name: `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow`, `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`, `effects`, `audio`, `platform`, `log`, `env`.
- Two contributions of one slot need different `order` values.
- `safeNode` is the path of a checkpoint node.
- A flow above 15 nodes is a warning. Split it into sub-flows of 7 to 15 nodes.

## Plugins

Registered in this order: `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow`; then the list `screen` a game spreads in: `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`; then the opt-in `effects`, `audio` and `platform` when the game adds them, `platform` last. `log` and `env` from `@moku-labs/common` are on every context as `ctx.log` and `ctx.env`. Configure with `createApp({ pluginConfigs: { <name>: { ... } } })`. Global config: `createApp({ config: { orientation, referenceSide } })`, defaults `"portrait"` and `1080`.

### time (Standard, no dependencies, no events)

The single `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Six phases in this order: `input`, `animate`, `layout`, `sync`, `signals`, `render`.
- API: `onFrame(phase, callback): () => void`, `snapshot(): Readonly<Time>`, `setScale(scale)`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `isPaused()`, `isRunning()`, `step(deltaMs)`, `wake()`.
- `Time` is `{ delta, elapsed, scale, frame, idle }` in scaled milliseconds.
- Idle cap: after `idleAfterMs` unscaled milliseconds without a `wake()` the loop runs at `idleFps` and `snapshot().idle` is true. `wake()` lifts it at once; `input`, `anim`, `flow`, `assets`, `scenes`, `text` and `ui` call it. `step(deltaMs)` is never capped.
- Config: `maxFps: 30 | 60 | 120` default `60`, `maxDeltaMs: number` default `50`, `idleFps: 0 | 30` default `30` (`0` turns the idle cap off), `idleAfterMs: number` default `2000`.
- In plain Bun there is no frame source. `isRunning()` is false and tests drive frames with `step`.

### lifecycle (Standard, depends on time)

The stack of pause reasons. The game is paused while the stack is not empty.
- API: `push(reason)`, `pop(reason)`, `reasons(): readonly PauseReason[]`, `isPaused()`.
- Named reasons: `"background"`, `"devtools"`, `"system-dialog"`, `"device-lost"`. Any other string is allowed.
- Event `lifecycle:changed`: `{ reason, action: "push" | "pop", reasons, paused, resumed }`. `resumed` is true only on the change that emptied the stack.
- No config.

### model (Very Complex, no dependencies)

The `session` tree and the save document `{ player, rng }`. Modules `store` and `rng`.
- `store`: `load()`, `snapshot(): { player, session, rng }` frozen, `begin(): Transaction`, `markRest()`, `markBarrier(txId)`, `rollback()`, `restore({ player, session?, rng? })`, `flush()`.
- `rng`: `peek(id): number | undefined`.
- `load()` hands the whole document to `provider.commit()` at once when it rewrote the save: a new player and a migrated save are stored before the first node runs. A save at the current version produces no commit.
- A game reads `app.model.store.snapshot()`. The runner calls the rest. A node never calls the model.
- Event `model:committed`: `{ roots: readonly ("player" | "session" | "rng")[]; cause: "edge" | "rollback" | "restore" | "load" }`.
- Config: `playerProvider: PlayerStateProvider | undefined` default `undefined` which means in-memory, `initialPlayer: Json` default `{}`, `initialSession: Json` default `{}`, `seed: "from-save" | number` default `"from-save"`, `schemaVersion: number` default `1`, `migrations: readonly Migration[]` default `[]`.
- `PlayerStateProvider`: `load(): Promise<{ state: Json; version: number } | null>`, `commit(patches, version): void`, `commitDurable(patches, txId, version): Promise<void>`, `flush(): Promise<void>`.
- `Migration` is `{ from: number; up(state: Json): Json }`. `up` of `from: n` produces version `n + 1`. It works on the whole save document.
- `SaveUnreadableError` has `savedVersion` and `schemaVersion`. `flow.run()` rejects with it when the save is newer, a step is missing, a step throws or the shape is wrong.

### clock (Standard, no dependencies, no events)

Trusted time as an input. Monotonic `now()` and one `elapsed` signal at the next due moment.
- API: `now()`, `scheduleAt(moment | undefined)`, `onElapsed(listener): () => void`, `poke()`, `dueAt()`.
- Config: `source: ClockSource | undefined` default `undefined` which means the system clock. `ClockSource` is `{ now(), setTimer(callback, delayMs), clearTimer(handle) }`.
- A node never touches the clock. It awaits `fx(schedule(moment))`. `flow` posts `{ type: "elapsed", payload: { now } }` into its inbox when the moment arrives and when the game resumes.

### flow (Very Complex, depends on time, lifecycle, model, clock)

The graph. Modules `runner`, `gate`, `inbox`, `fx`, `features`. Runner methods sit on the plugin root.
- Runner: `run(): Promise<void>`, `onEnter(stage: "load" | "scene", callback): () => void`, `walk(route, options?: { from?: Bookmark }): Promise<FlowState>`, `bookmark(): Bookmark`, `restore(bookmark): Promise<void>`, `describe(): FlowGraph`, `state(): FlowState`, `history(): readonly JournalEntry[]`, `setMode("live" | "fast")`.
- `gate.answer({ intent, payload? }): boolean` is the one entry of player answers. `gate.pointer(active)`. `gate.state(): { open, allowed, narrowed }`.
- `inbox.post({ type, payload? })` queues a world event. One entry per type. It is delivered only to a rest node whose `inbox` lists the type.
- `fx.handle(kind, handler, options?: { runInFast?: boolean }): () => void` registers the single handler of one effect kind. `fx.dispatch(descriptor)` is fire-and-forget. An awaited effect without a handler resolves `undefined` at once.
- `features.register(name, description)`, `features.all()`, `features.contributions(slotName)`.
- `FlowState` is `{ running, path, stack, pending: { fx?, gate? }, mode }`.
- `Bookmark` is `{ path, input, player, session, rng, graph, scene?, rest? }`. Serialisable. `scene` is written by the `game.bookmark` door and read by `game.restore`; `flow.restore` ignores it. `path` names a rest node, or the transit node that waits at the gate for an effect that takes answers (a `popup`, or a hand-written descriptor with `answers`); `rest: { path, input }` then names the rest point before it (left out when the graph started at that node or a restore entered it), and the state is the one committed when that node was entered. `restore` needs a running graph. A rest checkpoint is always accepted. Any other node is accepted only when the graph did not change since the bookmark; with another graph a transit bookmark is entered at `rest` instead when that is a checkpoint, and the log gets `flow:restore-fell-back`.
- `restore` of a rest node resolves when the node is entered. `restore` of a transit node runs it again from its start, so its effects before the gate play again, and resolves once its gate is open. The open gate is not the draw: the popup shows on the next frame. `restore` also resolves when the loop ends before the bookmark was entered, after a stop or a fatal error, and nothing is entered then.
- Events: `flow:edge` `{ flow, node, outcome, payload, next, patches: { doc, session }, index, now }` after the commit of an edge. `flow:rest` `{ path, checkpoint }`. `flow:error` `{ path, error, rolledBackTo, retry }`.
- Config: `mainFlow` default `undefined` and required before `run()`, `safeNode: string | undefined` default `undefined` which means the main flow's `start`, `retries` default `1`, `settleTimeoutMs` default `2000`, `journalLimit` default `500`.

### Screen plugins (V2, built)

`world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`. Each has a README at `src/plugins/<name>/README.md`; the root README lists their APIs, events and config. Rendering: WebGPU preferred, with Pixi's WebGL fallback.
- `app.scenes`: `current()` the mounted scene id, `expect(id)` the scene the next node without its own `scene` mounts, a rest node or a transit node in live mode (the restore door calls it; an unknown id throws). An `over` node takes it the same way, also over another mounted scene.
- `resource(name, defaults)` clones plain JSON defaults into every world. `resource(name, () => value)` calls the factory once per world on first read, so the value may hold a `Map` or a function: `const Looks = resource("boardLooks", () => ({ shown: new Map<World.Entity, { look: string }>() }))`. A system keeps its own state there; `snapshot()` leaves a value that is not JSON out.
- `app.world.projection.replace(spec)` swaps the spec of a registered projection; a mounted one runs its new `view` on the next frame. An unknown name throws. The caller is the dev hot swap.

### Interface plugins (V3, built)

A screen is a projection whose `view` returns JSX. The game's `tsconfig.json` sets `"jsx": "react-jsx"` and `"jsxImportSource": "@moku-labs/game"`; screens are `.tsx` files. There is no DOM and no React.

- Tags: `screen`, `layer`, `row`, `column`, `stack`, `spacer`, `panel` (swallows taps), `image` (`texture`, `fit?: "contain" | "cover" | "fill"`), `icon` (`name`, `fit?`), `text` (`content: string | Message`, or `bind={bind(Counter, "value")}` with `components={[Counter({ value })]}`; formats `int`, `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `duration`; `Countdown({ until })` with `bind(Countdown, "left", { format: "mm:ss" })` counts down to a `clock` moment; `style` is a text style key), `button` (`intent` + `payload`, or `local`, never both), `scroll` (`axis: "y"`; children for a short list, or the windowed form `rows`, `rowHeight`, `overscan?` (5), `row: index => node`; row state belongs in the model, a row that leaves the window loses its local state), `input` (a text field; its text lives in the component's `local`, see the ui README). Common props: `key`, `style`, `state: { active?, disabled?, selected? }`, `motion`, `components` (extra component values for the element's entity, such as a filter: `components={[Glow({ strength: 2 })]}`); containers take `hosts?: string[]` (projections drawn inside the element). Style adds `nineSlice`, `tint`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `scale`, `origin`, `fit: "contain"`; state variants `is: { hover, pressed, disabled, active, selected, covered }`. `popup(Component, props, { over })` stacks a popup over a kept one.
- Style vocabulary (`defineStyle`, plain data): flow `direction`, `wrap`, `justify`, `align`, `alignSelf`, `gap`, `grow`, `shrink`; box `padding`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `aspect`, `overflow`; position `position`, `left`, `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `reason`; visual `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `radius`, `alpha`; variants `is: { pressed?, disabled?, active?, selected? }` and `when: { portrait?, landscape?, tall?, wide? }`, each a partial style merged in when the flag holds. Lengths are reference units or `"safeArea.top" | "safeArea.right" | "safeArea.bottom" | "safeArea.left"`. No font size here: it comes from the text style.
- `defineComponent(name, { local?, outcomes?, view(props, local) })`. A component with `outcomes` is a popup: `await fx(popup(Component, props))` opens the gate for its outcomes and resolves with `{ intent, payload }` of the pressed button. A button with `local` writes into the nearest component instance; it never reaches the graph.
- `tr(key, params?)` returns a frozen `Message` `{ key, params }`; no locale is read at the call site. Strings live in `features/<feature>/strings/<locale>.json` as ICU MessageFormat 1 (`{n, plural, one {# order} other {# orders}}`, `select`, `selectordinal`, `number`, `date`, `time`; no skeletons, no `currency`). `bun run assets:keys` compiles them. A compiled module calls the root helpers `messageArgument(value, intl)` (an element stays an element part, a list goes through `Intl.ListFormat`, a number through `Intl.NumberFormat`, else text) and `messageDuration(ms)` (`95_000` gives `{ minutes: 1, seconds: 35 }`). `app.i18n`: `locale()`, `setLocale(locale)` (async, emits `i18n:locale-changed`), `format(message, locale?)` returns `Part[]`, `plain(message)` returns a string, `has(key)`, `locales()`, `replace(locale, messages)` (dev hot swap of a generated strings file). Config: `locale: "en"`, `fallback: "en"`, `locales: {}`.
- Text: `Text` component, `label({ text, style, at, anchor? })` for board text in a projection view, `defineTextStyles({ "hud.digits": { font, size, fill, bold?, italic?, stroke?, strokeWidth?, letterSpacing?, align?, wrap?, digits? } })` under the feature's `textStyles` key. Tags inside a string: `<b>`, `<i>`, `<color=#rrggbb>`, `<icon=key>`, `\<`, `\n`. Built-in styles `body` and `digits` from config `fonts: { body: "ui.font-body", digits: "ui.font-digits" }`. `app.text.measure(content, style)` gives the same numbers in a browser and in Bun. `app.text.replaceStyles(styles)` is the dev hot swap of a saved `defineTextStyles` value.
- Animation is data: `defineAnimation(id, { slots: { name: type<Anim.Target>() }, build: (slots, { at }) => Step })`. Steps: `sequence(...)`, `parallel(...)`, `stagger(items, ms, item => Step)`, `tween(target, Component, to, { ms, ease?, delayMs?, additive? })`, `set(target, Component, patch)`, `wait(ms)`, `mark(name)`, `frames(target, { keys, fps, loop? })`, `sfx(key, { bus? })`, `haptic(kind)`, `use(animation, slots, tools?)`, `spawn` (a temporary entity, flying coins, that the timeline despawns when it ends; see the anim README). `Frames({ keys, fps, loop, playing })` is a component that walks a sprite through its textures for the entity's whole life. A target is `{ projection, key }` or an entity. A node plays it with `await fx(play(animation, slots))`; in fast mode it finishes at once. `defineMotion({ states, transition?, on: { enter?, exit?, change? } })` builds the enter, exit and change hooks for a projection or the `motion` prop of a tag. Events `anim:mark` `{ animation, mark }` and `anim:finished` `{ animation }`. `app.anim.replace(definition)` is the dev hot swap: the next `play` builds the new tree. A system cannot `require` a plugin, so it plays through the resource `AnimPlayer`: `res(AnimPlayer).play(animation, slots)` returns the same handle as `app.anim.play`, and the registered animation of `animation.id` wins, so a hot swap reaches the system. Play on a change, never every frame; from phase `input` the tree moves in `animate` of the same frame. Before `anim` starts it throws `[game] AnimPlayer is not ready: anim has not started.` Config `maxTracks: 2000`.
- Audio is opt-in: `plugins: [...screen, audioPlugin]`. `fx(sfx("orders.complete"))` resolves when the sound started. `await fx(music("board.theme"))` cross-fades; `music(null)` fades out; a scene's `music` key switches the track on `scenes:changed`. Buses `master`, `music`, `sfx`. Volumes come from the committed player: config `volumes: player => (player as Player).settings.audio`, applied on every `model:committed`. `app.audio`: `setVolume(bus, value)`, `volume(bus)`, `mute(bus, on)`, `muted(bus)`, `unlocked()`, `journal()` (the last started sounds, empty unless config `journal` is above 0). Config: `buses: { master: 1, music: 0.6, sfx: 1 }`, `musicFadeMs: 600`, `volumes`, `context`, `journal: 0`, `music: "decode" | "stream"` default `"decode"` (gapless buffer; `"stream"` is an `<audio>` element, less memory, a gap at every loop), `session: "ambient" | "playback" | "auto"` default `"ambient"` (iOS only: ambient mixes with other apps and obeys the silent switch). Without `audio` every `sfx` and `music` effect resolves `undefined` at once, so the same node runs in a game with no sound.
- `app.ui`: `tree()` the live screen as plain data (a text node carries `content`, the words it draws after `tr()` and `bind`; a text field carries `value`), `find(key)` the entity of a keyed element, `fill(key, value)` types into the text field with that `key`, `lint()` tap targets under `tapTargetPt` (default `44`), text that overflows in some locale, absolute elements without `reason`. Config: `tapTargetPt: 44`, `breakpoints: { tall: 2, wide: 1.5 }`. `ui` emits only the dev global event `ui:hot-swap`, see "Hot swap".

```tsx
// features/hud/view.tsx
import type { Anim } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { Transform, mark, sequence, sfx, tween, type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineAnimation, defineComponent, defineFeature, defineTextStyles, projection, tr } from "../../state";

export const hud = projection({
  name: "hud",
  layer: "ui",
  from: player => ({ coins: player.coins }),
  view: hud => (
    <row key="bar" style={{ gap: 16, padding: { top: "safeArea.top", left: 24, right: 24 }, width: "100%", height: 120 }}>
      <text key="coins" style="hud.digits" content={tr("hud.coins", { n: hud.coins })} />
      <button key="settings" intent="openSettings" style={{ width: 96, height: 96 }}><icon name="hud.gear" /></button>
    </row>
  )
});

export const RewardPopup = defineComponent("RewardPopup", {
  outcomes: { claim: type<{ orderId: string }>() },
  view: (props: { orderId: string; gold: number }) => (
    <panel key="reward" style={{ nineSlice: "ui.panel", direction: "column", gap: 16, padding: 32, width: 600, height: 400, fit: "contain" }}>
      <text key="gold" style="hud.digits" content={String(props.gold)} />
      <button key="claim" intent="claim" payload={{ orderId: props.orderId }} style={{ width: 240, height: 88 }}>
        <text content={tr("common.claim")} />
      </button>
    </panel>
  )
});

export const popCoins = defineAnimation("hud.popCoins", {
  slots: { coins: type<Anim.Target>() },
  build: ({ coins }) => sequence(tween(coins, Transform, { scale: 1.2 }, { ms: 120 }), tween(coins, Transform, { scale: 1 }, { ms: 200 }), sfx("hud.coins"), mark("done"))
});

export const hudFeature = defineFeature("hud", {
  projections: [hud],
  ui: [RewardPopup],
  animations: [popCoins],
  textStyles: defineTextStyles({ "hud.digits": { font: "ui.font-digits", size: 40, fill: 0xffe082, digits: true } }),
  strings: { en: () => import("../../generated/strings.en") }
});

// features/orders/deliver.ts — the popup and the choreography are effects the node awaits
import { play, type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineNode, popup } from "../../state";
import { popCoins, RewardPopup } from "../hud/view";

export const deliver = defineNode({
  outcomes: { claimed: type<{ orderId: string }>() },
  run: async ({ player, fx, out }) => {
    const answer = (await fx(popup(RewardPopup, { orderId: "o1", gold: 5 }))) as { intent: "claim"; payload: { orderId: string } };

    player.coins += 5;
    await fx(play(popCoins, { coins: { projection: "hud", key: "coins" } }));
    return out.claimed({ orderId: answer.payload.orderId });
  }
});
```

### effects (V5, Complex, opt-in)

Cosmetic rendering extras as data, drawn by `effectsPlugin`: `plugins: [...screen, effectsPlugin]`. Nothing here enters `model`, the journal or a save. Headless it draws nothing. The full reference is `src/plugins/effects/README.md`.
- Particles: `defineEmitter(id, config)` returns frozen data a feature lists under `emitters`. Required: `textures` (1 to 16 asset keys of one atlas page) and exactly one of `burst` (an integer, emitted once) and `rate` (particles per second while `active`). Optional with defaults: `lifeMs`, `speed`, `angle`, `gravity`, `drag`, `spin`, `shape` (`point`, `circle`, `rect`, `ring`), `scale`, `alpha`, `tint` (each `{ from, to }`), `space` (`"world"` or `"local"`), `prewarmMs`, `maxParticles` (`256`), `blend` (`"normal"` or `"add"`). A mistake throws at definition.
- The `Emitter({ effect, active })` component on an entity runs an emitter: `generator: item => [Sprite({ texture: "board.generator" }), Emitter({ effect: "fx.steam" })]`. `effect: ""` draws nothing. Particles step in the `animate` phase, so they freeze while paused and a fast walk emits nothing. Their random source is seeded, never `Math.random` and never the model's rng.
- Filters: `defineFilter(id, { wgsl, glsl, uniforms?, passes?, padding? })` returns a component type a feature lists under `filters`. Both bodies are required: `wgsl` is the WGSL `fn mainFragment` and reads a uniform as `fu.amount`; `glsl` is GLSL ES 3.0 `void main()` that sets `finalColor` and reads a uniform as `amount`. A uniform is a number (tweenable), `{ color: 0xffd700 }` or an array of 2 to 4 numbers. Every filter component also has `enabled: true` and `order: 0`. A filter covers the entity's subtree; on a ui element it goes in the `components` prop.
- Built-in filters: `Glow`, `Outline`, `Blur`, `ColorMatrix`, `Noise`, `Displacement` (`map` is an asset key), `Alpha`. A motion hook tweens them like any component: `view.tween(Glow, { strength: 0 }, { ms: 200 })`.
- API: `app.effects.stats()` returns `{ particles, emitters, filters, renderPasses }`; headless every number is 0.
- Config: `maxParticles: 3000` and `maxPasses: 24`, each warns once per crossing; `phone: "auto"`; `blur: { quality: 2, phoneResolution: 0.5 }`.
- With `emitters: "fx.starsBurst" | "fx.steam"` in the `defineGame` types, the `defineEmitter` id and `Emitter.effect` are checked by the compiler; `textures` and `Displacement.map` are checked against the asset keys. No events. Depends on `flow`, `world`, `renderer`, `assets`, `anim`.

### platform (V6, Standard, opt-in)

The phone as a provider, last in the array: `plugins: [...screen, effectsPlugin, audioPlugin, platformPlugin]` with `pluginConfigs: { platform: { provider, keepAwake: true } }`. `game.screen()` composes it and takes the provider as its `platform` seam. A game imports no native package: the engine page builds the provider from the `system` list of `config.ts` through `@moku-labs/game/app/system`, and turns keep-awake on when the list names `keepAwake`. The full reference is `src/plugins/platform/README.md`.
- `PlatformProvider` has six members: `onPause(fn)`, `onResume(fn)`, `onBack(fn)` (each returns its remover), `haptic(kind)`, `keepAwake(on)`, `exit()`. Pause and resume push and pop the `"background"` reason of `lifecycle`. A provider method that throws is logged, never thrown into the frame.
- Back chain, `app.platform.back(): BackResult`. First an Escape press: a popup with an `escape` button closes, `"popup"`. Then `flow.gate.answer({ intent: "back" })` when the resting node lists `back`, `"intent"`. Then `provider.exit()`, `"exit"`. Without a provider `"none"`.
- `app.platform.exit()`: the last step of the Back chain alone, `provider.exit()`, for a Leave button: `ctx.require(flowPlugin).fx.handle("exit", () => ctx.require(platformPlugin).exit())`. A throw is logged; without a provider it does nothing.
- Haptics: `await fx(haptic("success"))` in a node, or `haptic("light")` as a timeline step. The kinds are `HAPTIC_KINDS`: `light`, `medium`, `heavy`, `selection`, `success`, `warning`, `error`. A fast walk is silent.
- Config: `provider: undefined`, which leaves the plugin inert: a `haptic` effect resolves at once, so the same node runs on the web and headless. `keepAwake: false`.
- No events. Depends on `lifecycle`, `flow`, `input`.

## Game plugins and events

A game plugin is `createPlugin(name, { depends: [flowPlugin], hooks: ctx => ({ "flow:edge": payload => { ... } }) })`. The root README has the full example in its Events section.

A plugin that owns a resource stores it in its state and frees it in `onStop: ({ state }) => …` (core 1.6: `onStop` receives `{ global, config, state }`). A throwing `onStop` makes `app.stop()` reject. A hook that throws never stops the game: the engine writes the error entry `"game: a hook failed"` to the log (`app.log.trace()`), through the framework `onError(error, core)` of core 1.7. A game can pass its own `onError: (error, ctx) => …` to `createApp`; the kernel calls both.

## Doors for the editor

Two subpaths, neither on the root (V4). An editor, MCP tools and e2e scripts reach a running game through them; `docs/doors.md` in the engine repository has the full catalogue.

- `@moku-labs/game/inspect`: `read(app, source, input?)` reads once; `watch(app, source, input, fn)` reads on the `signals` phase when the source changes and returns the stop function; `defineSource`; the frozen catalogue `sources`; the types `Source`, `InputSchema`, `InputOf`. Every source only reads, so the door is safe in a production build. Keys of `sources`: `graph`, `position`, `history`, `tainted`, `cheats`, `model`, `entities`, `projections`, `ui`, `locate`, `render`, `sounds`, `audioMuted`, `effects`, `assets`, `log`, `explain`, `diff`, `schema`, `at`; their ids are `game.<key>`. `locate` takes `{ key }` (a ui element) or `{ target }` (a view by projection key) and answers its box in CSS px, the numbers Playwright clicks. `at` takes `{ x, y }` in CSS px and lists the views under that point, topmost first. `explain` takes `{ entity }` and answers that entity in full, `undefined` for a stale id. `diff` takes `{ from, to }` frames and answers what changed per entity; it throws in a production build and for a frame outside the last 120. `schema` lists every component and tag type the world met, with the JSON kind of each field. `audioMuted` answers whether the master bus is muted. `sounds` throws `[game] The source game.sounds needs audioPlugin.`, `audioMuted` throws `[game] The source game.audioMuted needs audioPlugin.` and `effects` throws `[game] The source game.effects needs effectsPlugin.` when that plugin is not installed; the editor lists such a source as not installed.
- `@moku-labs/game/control`: `run(app, command, input?)` resolves `{ value, state }`, `state` being `{ path, frame, tainted }`; `defineCommand`; `controlRefused`; the frozen catalogue `commands`; the types `Command`, `Ran`. Keys of `commands`: `answer`, `tap`, `drag`, `key`, `fill`, `walk`, `bookmark`, `restore`, `step`, `pause`, `resume`, `capture`, `debug`, `reducedMotion`, `timeScale`, `mute`, `trace`. `capture` resolves `{ png }`, and `{ png, legend }` with `legend: true`; `undefined` while the renderer is inert. `timeScale` takes `{ scale }`; 0 freezes game time while the frames keep running. `mute` takes `{ muted }`, mutes the master bus and answers the flag. Without `audioPlugin` it throws `[game] The command game.mute needs audioPlugin.` `trace` takes `{ path }`, a list of views by projection key, and answers whether the gate took the answer.
- Commands run in dev builds only. Only `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__ === true` turns the dev build on: `moku-game dev` defines it `true` and sets the global in `.moku/dev.ts`, `moku-game build` defines it `false`; a game without the shell uses a bundler `define`; a test uses `vi.stubGlobal("__MOKU_GAME_DEV__", true)`. Otherwise `run` throws `[game] Control commands run in dev builds only.`
- A command's effect is `read`, `route`, `cosmetic`, `cheat` or `raw`. A `cheat` or `raw` command taints the session and is journaled; read it with `sources.tainted` and `sources.cheats`. Of the base commands only `restore` is `raw`. `bookmark` answers `flow.bookmark()` plus `scene`, the mounted scene; `restore` calls `scenes.expect(scene)` before `flow.restore`, so a bookmark at a popup restores the scene under it, also on a page that shows another scene. A bookmark taken while an effect that takes answers waits names the waiting transit node (`info/show` in the mini game) and carries `rest`; `restore` of it answers once that node's gate is open, with `pending.gate` in its value, and the popup shows on the next frame.
- A game's own: `defineSource({ id, title, input, changes, read })` with `changes` `"frame"`, `"commit"` or `"edge"`, and `defineCommand({ id, title, input, effect, run })`. The id is camelCase words joined by dots, at least two: `dice.rolls`. An input schema maps field names to `"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"` or `"json"`; a trailing `?` makes one optional. A command body starts with `if (typeof __MOKU_GAME_DEV__ === "undefined" || !__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) throw controlRefused();`. Keep them in `.dev` modules that only the dev page and the tests import: the editor's dev page (`preparePage` with agents) imports every `**/*.dev.ts`, `moku-game build` none.

## Project index

`@moku-labs/game/project` maps every engine id of a game to anchors (a path plus a binding, a key or a component), never to line numbers; `find` reads the line from the file on disk at the call. `typescript` (`>=5.5`) is an optional peer: a game that uses the index adds it as a dev dependency. Nothing is persisted. The contract is in `docs/project-index.md`.

```ts
import { openProject } from "@moku-labs/game/project";

const project = await openProject({ root: "tests/fixtures/mini-game" });
(await project.find("node:infoPopup/count"))[0]?.line; // 7, in "nodes/count.ts"
const stop = project.watch((index, change) => refresh(index.revision, change.moved));
stop();
project.close();
```

- `openProject({ root, manifest?, tsconfig?, debounceMs? })` resolves `ProjectApi`: `index` (frozen, replaced per batch), `find(key)` (a `Found[]`: the anchor plus `line`, `range` `[startLine, startCol, endLine, endCol]` 1-based with an exclusive end column, `hash`, and `broken: true` when the file does not parse now), `watch(onIndex)` (one call per batch that changed bytes, with `(index, change)`; returns the stop function), `changed(path)` (re-index one root-relative path now, no watch call), `close()`. Without `typescript` it rejects with `[game] The project index needs the "typescript" package.`
- Aliases: the index follows imports through the `compilerOptions.paths` of `tsconfig.json` at the root (or the root-relative `tsconfig`), `extends` included, as TypeScript does, so `@core/kit`, `@shared` and `@features/home` reach their files. `index.tsconfig` names that file when it holds `paths`. `@moku-labs/game` stays a package. A tsconfig edit rebuilds the aliases in the next watch batch.
- Keys: `flow:<id>`, `node:<flow>/<node>` (every entry of a `nodes` table: node, sub-flow, slot), `feature:<id>`, `scene:<id>`, `projection:<name>`, `emitter:<id>`, `textStyle:<key>`, `style:<path>#<binding>` (a module-level `const` of `defineStyle`), `style:<path>#<function>` (every `defineStyle` call inside a module-level function or function-valued const; `find` answers each call) and `style:<path>#<function>.<property>` (a call under an object property there; a style in a class, an object const or at module scope stays unresolved), `component:<Name>` (in a `.tsx` file a module-level upper-case `function Name` or function-valued `const Name`; anywhere `defineComponent("Name", …)`, bound to its const; `uses` are the files that render `<binding>`), `jsx:<key>`. Definers are recognised by binding from the kit's `defineGame()` destructure, renamed imports too. A non-literal id goes to `index.unresolved` with the reason, never guessed.
- JSX keys are patterns: literal text stays, same-file consts and functions are followed, a key-carrying prop (`id`, or a name that ends in `Key`) becomes a hole of its name, `props.id` reads `{id}` and `props.amountKey` reads `{amountKey}`, any other hole `*`. `` key={`${id}Picture`} `` reads `jsx:card*Picture` (stem `card`); `id="settingsBoard"` on `<Signboard>` reads `jsx:settingsBoard` (kind `idProp`, component `Signboard`, prop `id`); `amountKey="giftReward"` on `<Amount>` reads `jsx:giftReward` (prop `amountKey`). `find("jsx:settingsBoardClose")`, a key `game.locate` reports, answers the `{id}Close` pattern of the kit and the `id=` prop that fills it; a hole takes only the props of its own name.
- `ProjectChange` is `{ revision, files, moved: [{ key, from, to }], removed }`. A broken file keeps its last good keys and gets `files[path].state === "broken"`. Paths are root-relative POSIX; a path that leaves the root is refused.
- CLI: `moku-game-index --root <dir> where <key>` prints `<path>:<line>` per place (exit 1 for an unknown key); `--json` prints the index; `--check` exits 1 on a broken file or a key in conflict and lists the unresolved items as info. With a tsconfig, `--check` also prints the aliases line, `aliases: tsconfig.json, 8 patterns`, or `aliases: none (no tsconfig paths)`. `--root` is required, `--manifest <path>` and `--tsconfig <path>` are root-relative.

## Hot swap

Dev only. A save of a view file swaps the module in the running page: same state, same node, no reload. `moku-game dev` lists the plugin first in its `.moku/bunfig.toml` and runs the server in the game root, so a game sets nothing; `moku-game build` never loads it. A game with a server of its own lists it in its own `bunfig.toml`:

```toml
[serve.static]
plugins = ["@moku-labs/game/hot"]
```

- View files swap: `.tsx`, `styles.ts`, `view.ts`, `animations.ts`, `effects.ts`, `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`. On the layered layout also any `.ts` directly in a kind folder: `styles/`, `motion/`, `effects/`, `views/`, `world/projections/`, `world/layout/`, in a feature or in `shared/`. Styles, components, function components, projections of a registered name, animations, text styles, emitters and strings. Under `moku-game dev` or the editor's `watchKeys` a save of a strings JSON compiles by itself and its output swaps, a new key too. A game with a server of its own runs `bun run assets:keys` after a strings JSON edit; its output is what swaps.
- Logic files reload the page: `rules/`, `nodes/`, `flows/`, `state.ts`, `tables.ts`, `kit.ts`, a feature `index.ts`, `world/components/`, `world/systems/`. A view file that exports a scene, system, ECS component, filter, flow, node, feature, plugin, a new projection or a new animation is refused: `ui` logs `ui:hot-refused` and throws, and Bun reloads the page.
- Asset files, under `moku-game dev` on the raw files or the editor's `watchKeys`: a texture, a bitmap font (`.fnt` or its page) or a sound saved with new bytes swaps in the loaded bundles, same key, no reload. The keys watch writes `.moku/assets-stamp.ts` `{ files, changed }`, the hot plugin lets the page accept it, and `assets` reads the changed files again. A new, removed or renamed asset file, a changed nine-slice tag too, reloads the page. So does a replace that fails. Not with `--packed`, not in a built game. A bundle that is not loaded reads the new bytes on its next load. A sound that is playing plays on; a running particle effect of a replaced texture starts again.
- A swap logs `ui:hot-swap` and emits the global event `ui:hot-swap` `{ file, module }`. `effects` hooks it for emitters, `assets` for the stamp module.
- Event `assets:replaced` `{ bundle, keys }`, dev only: `assets` emits it once per bundle after an asset swap. `keys` are the asset keys with new bytes; `app.assets.texture(key)`, `font(key)` and `audio(key)` answer the new object and the old textures are destroyed. `text`, `effects` and `audio` hook it; a game plugin that built something from a key hooks it with `depends: [assetsPlugin]` and builds it again.
- Another layout, on a server of the game's own: `export default hot({ include, exclude })` from the game's `hot.ts`, listed as `plugins = ["./hot.ts"]`.
- Keep a view helper in the module of the projection that uses it. A function another module stored into an object at load time keeps the old version.

## Fonts

The package ships one MSDF body font: `fonts/font-body.fnt` and `fonts/font-body.png` (Pangolin Regular) with `fonts/LICENSE.txt` (SIL Open Font License 1.1). Copy it into the game; a path in `node_modules` is not an asset key, the scanner reads keys only from `features/<feature>/assets/` and from the layers of `--layer`. The licence goes next to `assets/`, not inside it.

```bash
mkdir -p src/features/ui/assets
cp node_modules/@moku-labs/game/fonts/font-body.* src/features/ui/assets/
cp node_modules/@moku-labs/game/fonts/LICENSE.txt src/features/ui/LICENSE-fonts.txt
bun run assets:keys
```

The scanner keys it `ui.font-body`, which is the `text` config default `fonts.body`, so the built-in style `body` works with no config. No `digits` font ships: a game that uses the style `digits` brings `ui.font-digits` itself.

## Testing entry

Exports of `@moku-labs/game/testing`: `createHeadless`, `runRepro`, `stepFrames`, `fakeClock`, `memory`, `saveOf`, `isolate`, `stub`. The visual tests `defineVisualTest`, `runVisualTests`, `parseVisualArgv` come from `@moku-labs/game/visual`, node and bun only (see `docs/testing.md` in the engine repository).

- `createHeadless(app): Promise<HeadlessGame>`. Pass an app that is not started. It sets mode `"fast"`, awaits `app.start()`, starts `flow.run()` unless the app's `onStart` already did, and resolves when the loop rests for the first time: `game.state().path` already names the first rest node. A fatal error of `run()` rejects the call.
- `HeadlessGame`: `walk(route): Promise<FlowState>`, `answer(answer): boolean`, `state()`, `history()`, `stop()`. `walk` and `stop` throw a fatal error of the loop again when the headless runner owns `run()`.
- `Flow.RouteStep` is `{ at: string; intent: string; payload?: Json }` or `{ at: string; result: { outcome: string; payload?: Json } }`. `at` is the path of a rest node. The `result` form substitutes the result of a sub-flow at that path.
- `runRepro(app, { player, session?, rng?, checkpoint?, route }): Promise<{ path: string[]; player; session }>`. The app keeps running. Stop it with `app.stop()`.
- `stepFrames(app, count, deltaMs)` calls `app.time.step(deltaMs)` `count` times.
- `fakeClock(start = 0)`: a `ClockSource` with `advance(ms)` and `set(moment)`. `advance` fires due timers synchronously.
- `memory(fixture?)`: in-memory `PlayerStateProvider` with `calls`, the list of every call. It applies the patches it is committed to the document it holds, so a second app over the same instance reads what the first one wrote. `saveOf(player, seed = 1)` builds a `SaveDoc`.

```ts
import type { Flow } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { createHeadless } from "@moku-labs/game/testing";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import game from "./index";

const rollOnce: Flow.RouteStep = { at: "home", intent: "roll" };

it("plays two rolls without a screen", async () => {
  const { app } = game.headless({ seed: 42 });
  const run = await createHeadless(app);

  const state = await run.walk([rollOnce, rollOnce]);

  expect(state.path).toBe("home");
  expect(app.model.store.snapshot().session).toEqual({ rolls: 2 });

  await run.stop();
});
```

Isolated feature tests play one feature without the rest of the game:

- `isolate(feature, options): (seams?) => App`. It composes `options.shared` and the feature as `logicOnly`, then `options.plugins`. The feature's `flow` becomes the node `as` (default `flow.id`) of a harness main flow `isolated`, so paths read as in the game. Options: `flow`, `player` (both required), `as?`, `shared?`, `stubs?`, `plugins?`, `session?` (`{}`), `seed?` (`1`). The factory takes the seams of one app, `player`, `session`, `seed`, `clock`; they win over the options. Pass the app to `createHeadless`.
- `stub(outcome, payload?)`: `stub("closed")` is `{ kind: "stub", outcome: "closed" }`. `stubs: { <node name>: stub(...) }` replaces that node or sub-flow of `flow`; it ends at once with the outcome.
- A node that is not stubbed runs for real, the flow of another feature too.
- A stub is a sub-flow, so a route may still substitute it for one visit: `{ at: "board/energy", result: { outcome: "watch" } }`.
- A checkpoint compacts `history()`: assert on `state()` or on `flow:edge` events.
- Every exit of a flow with outcomes lands on the rest node `exited`; `{ at: "exited", intent: "again" }` enters the flow once more.
- A wrong stub key or outcome does not compile, and throws at run time: `[game] isolate: no node "enrgy" in flow "board".`

```ts
import { createHeadless, isolate, stub } from "@moku-labs/game/testing";
import { homeFeature } from "./features/home";
import { mainFlow } from "./flows/main";

// The mini game: home opens the popup info, here stubbed with its outcome ok.
const homeOnly = isolate(homeFeature, { flow: mainFlow, stubs: { info: stub("ok") }, player: { count: 0 } });
const game = await createHeadless(homeOnly());

game.state().path; // "main/home": the harness holds the flow under its id
await game.walk([{ at: "main/home", intent: "info" }]); // the stub ends with ok at once
game.state().path; // "main/home"
await game.stop();
```

For timers, take the clock of `game.headless()`, a `fakeClock(startMoment)`: call `clock.advance(ms)`, then yield the microtask queue before reading the state. The seed is the definition's, else 42; `game.headless({ seed: 7 })` pins another. The headless app composes `logicOnly` of `headless.features`. An app made with `createApp` by hand passes `clock: { source: fakeClock(1_000_000) }`, `model: { seed: 42 }` and `plugins: [feature.logicOnly]` itself.

## File layout of a game

```
index.ts          export default defineGameApp({ ... }): the game as one data object
config.ts         export default { page, native?, system?, save?, assets? } satisfies GameConfig
core/             the kit (the defineGame call) and its types
shared/           the shared layer
features/<f>/     one feature: flow/, rules/, views/, styles/, motion/, world/, assets/, strings/
plugins/          the game's own plugins
generated/        what moku-game keys writes: assets.ts, the strings, manifest.json
tests/            the tests; tests/scenarios/<name>.ts are the saves of ?player=<name>
.moku/            what moku-game writes, ignored by git
```

Rules are pure functions in `rules/`: no engine import, no clock, no random. The tsconfig aliases are `@core/*`, `@shared`, `@features/*`. The lint rules `layer-imports`, `feature-door` and `test-suffix`, the hot kind folders, the `assets.layers` of `config.ts` and the project index follow the layers `core/`, `shared/`, `features/` and `plugins/`.

The worked example is the merge game in moku-labs/demos (https://github.com/moku-labs/demos), written on the public API only, with its e2e and visual tests. The engine repository keeps a smaller fixture, `tests/fixtures/mini-game/` (`index.ts`, `config.ts`, `tests/scenarios/ready.ts`, one rest node, one popup flow, two features), which is not in the npm package. A feature with a screen adds `view.tsx` (projections and components), `animations.ts` and `strings/<locale>.json`. Each plugin has a README: `src/plugins/<name>/README.md` for `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow`, `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`, `audio`, `effects`, `platform`. Moku Core specification: https://github.com/moku-labs/core/tree/main/specification
